get.description: Liveness: the process is up. Does not touch any dependency.
Readiness: every dependency answers. 503 if any check fails or times out.

The admin behind the token: the id and the roles in it. Nothing is looked up, because
admins live in identity-api; this is the first admin endpoint and a check for Phase 3.

card and a Publishing card with figures that open the module's pages, and the latest
decisions. The same counts as `GET /v1/admin/summary`, in the shell's shared shape.

Outbox events, paged, without their bodies. Newest first; with no `status` filter the

waited (also on `/ready`, for monitoring).
One event with its body and what happened to it.

post.description:
Puts a `dead` event back to `pending` (its attempts start again, and the log records the
admin). The worker sends it in its turn: it never overtakes an earlier version of the same
aggregate that is still waiting. `409 invalid_outbox_status` for any other status.

get.description:
The queue: what vendors have submitted, filterable and paged. Pending reviews come oldest
first, so the one that has waited longest is on top; other statuses come newest first.

One review with the version under review, the version it is compared with, **the fields
that changed**, and its audit trail.

post.description:
Approves a pending review: a brand profile version becomes the published one (the old one
is superseded), a product revision becomes the live revision. All in one transaction, with one
audit event naming the reviewer from the token and what changed. `409 stale_review` if the
submission is not the `version` the reviewer saw (or is no longer waiting, or a newer profile
version is already live); `409 review_already_decided` if it was decided first.

Rejects a pending review. A reason is required (`422` without one) and the vendor sees it.
Same `409`s as approving. A live product stays live: only the rejected revision is turned
down.

get.description:

the queue.

Vendors, paged. Pending applications come oldest first, so the one that has waited
longest is on top; other statuses come newest first.

post.description:
Approves a pending, rejected or suspended vendor, and tells it by email. `409
invalid_status_transition` for one that is already approved.

get.description: A brand's commission. `404` for an unknown vendor.

post.description:
Agrees the brand's waiting proposal. `409 no_proposal` when none waits;
`409 commission_changed` when it is not the `proposed_bps` sent.

Sends the waiting proposal back with a note (10 to 600 characters) the brand sees. The
agreed rate, if any, stays. `409 no_proposal` when none waits.

Sets the agreed rate directly (for example agreed on a call), whatever was proposed; an
optional note up to 600 characters. `409 vendor_not_eligible` for a rejected application.

Rejects a **pending** vendor (a reason is required, and the vendor is told it). Ends every
session of the vendor at once. `409 invalid_status_transition` otherwise: an approved vendor
is suspended, not rejected.

get.description:
A vendor's store details as the vendor sees them: payouts masked (bank, last four digits
or a masked UPI ID), never the number. `404` for an unknown vendor.

post.description:
Suspends an **approved** vendor (a reason is required, and the vendor is told it). Ends
every session of the vendor at once: it cannot sign in or refresh, and its access tokens stop
working immediately. Approving it again reinstates it. `409 invalid_status_transition`
otherwise.
